investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (curl, plain HTTP GET) against the venue's official 'Upcoming events' page found only an empty, JS-populated calendar shell. Level 2 STRUCTURAL escalation — fetching the page's own referenced JS bundle (a plain HTTP GET of a public .js file, no execution) and reading the plain REST endpoint URL strings it constructs — found a real, public, unauthenticated WordPress REST route this theme itself exposes, then confirmed it directly with a second plain HTTP GET.

probe_history.reason:
A plain curl GET of https://www.olympiahall.com/en/upcoming-events/ returns real static HTML for the page shell (header/footer/filters), but the actual listing container is genuinely empty in the response: `
...
` with zero event cards anywhere in the retained bytes. No JSON-LD, NUXT/NEXT data blob, or repeated static event card markup is present either.

Fetched the page's own referenced compiled JS bundle (https://www.olympiahall.com/wp-content/themes/olympia/dist/app.js, a plain HTTP GET of a public static file, no execution) and found it literally constructs `window.location.origin + "/wp-json/olympia/v1/events-calendar/?lang=" + e` and `.../wp-json/df-elastic-search/v1/search-evenements/?lang=" + e`, plus a `formatPeriods()` function building a `filter_periods[0][begin_date]=YYYY-MM-DD` query parameter — all read directly as literal strings in the bundle, never guessed. Calling the second endpoint directly with that exact parameter shape returned 124 real, current, full event records (title/permalink/genre/begin_date/end_date/price). Level 2 fully answered the investigation question; no browser/headless step was needed.

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'Concerts & shows in Paris | L'Olympia' at the venue's own domain olympiahall.com. The page's own footer directly self-identifies: 'L'Olympia / 28 boulevard des Capucines / 75009 Paris' — matching the assigned venue reference exactly, a self-consistent first-party artifact.

site_classification.platform: WordPress with a bespoke theme (olympia) and two custom REST namespaces (`olympia/v1`, `df-elastic-search/v1`) — the client-rendered programmation page calls its own theme's public REST route to populate the listing. Never HEADLESS_REQUIRED: the endpoint is reachable and fully data-complete via a plain HTTP GET with no browser/JS execution, discovered only by reading the bundle's own literal endpoint-construction strings (Level 2 STRUCTURAL), not by observing rendered network traffic.

title.notes: Each record's own `post_title` field, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each record's own `meta.begin_date` field (e.g. '2026-09-03 20:30:00'), stated directly, full date always present.

time.value: 20:30 (Europe/Paris, floating local — no explicit UTC offset anywhere in this field)
time.notes: The time-of-day portion of `meta.begin_date`, stated directly. No timezone offset is ever appended in the sampled data — recorded honestly as FLOATING_LOCAL.

end.notes: Each record's own distinct `meta.end_date` field, stated directly (e.g. Baby Keem: same calendar day, '2026-09-03 23:25:00'; a genuine multi-day record, 'Jarry', shows begin_date '2026-09-09' and a distinct end_date '2026-09-11' — a real 3-day run, both directly stated, not derived).

venue_location.notes: Not stated per-record as a discrete field. This source represents exactly one physical venue (L'Olympia, 28 Boulevard des Capucines) — consistent with the badehaus-berlin-01/zenner-berlin-01 precedent, venue identity is intended to resolve via source_id at activation time.

source_record_id.notes: Each record's own numeric WordPress post `ID` field (this source's 'evenement' custom post type's own database identity), stated directly and distinct from the human-readable permalink slug.

event_url.notes: Each record's own `permalink` field, stated directly — this venue's own first-party event page.

price.notes: Each record's own `meta.gamme_de_prix` field, stated directly as a ready-made price-range string.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, and the page's own footer directly stating the venue's full name and address).
Level 1 was genuinely insufficient (empty, JS-populated calendar shell) and honestly recorded as such before escalating.

Level 2 STRUCTURAL escalation (reading the page's own referenced JS bundle's literal endpoint-construction strings, then confirming with a plain HTTP GET) found a real, public, unauthenticated REST route — acquisition_class PUBLIC_JSON_API, a resolved supported class.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: one request exposing 124 real, current, full event records at once.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own numeric WordPress post ID, directly present on every record.

This source's own genre taxonomy directly distinguishes music genres from its one non-music value ('Comedy') — isMusicRecord() in ingestion/olympia-paris/observation-adapter.mjs implements this as an explicit, never-silent filter using the source's own classification, never a keyword guess.

PARIS_BESPOKE: no existing collector family in this project matches this exact custom REST-plugin JSON shape; a new, small, bespoke module was written (ingestion/olympia-paris/observation-adapter.mjs).
DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence retained (tests/olympia-paris.test.mjs, 5 passing assertions re-parsing the retained fixture deterministically, including the multi-day case).

evidence.description: The venue's own official 'Upcoming events' page, byte-retained in full (56,683 bytes), proving Level 1 insufficiency: an empty `.c-calendar__days` container and `.t-programmation.loading--` state, zero event cards in the static response.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution)

evidence.description: A bounded, disclosed excerpt (900 bytes) of the venue's own compiled theme JS bundle (originally 489,342 bytes, a minified webpack bundle), retaining only the literal code constructing the REST endpoint URLs (`wp-json/olympia/v1/events-calendar/`, `wp-json/df-elastic-search/v1/search-evenements/`) and the `filter_periods[0][begin_date]` query-parameter shape. The retained excerpt itself is a verbatim substring of the original file (not re-parsed/re-serialized); the surrounding ~488KB of unrelated minified JS was dropped, disclosed honestly here.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution — a static .js file fetched as plain text, never executed)

evidence.description: Byte-retained raw response (2,668 bytes) of the `olympia/v1/events-calendar` REST route for August 2026, confirming it returns only per-day `has_event` booleans, not event detail fields — explaining why the OTHER endpoint (`df-elastic-search/v1/search-evenements`) is this source's actual data path for facts.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication)

evidence.description: A bounded, disclosed, real subset (12 records, 7,225 bytes) of this endpoint's actual live response (originally 124 matching records across 7 pages, 277,649 bytes for one page of 20). Each retained record keeps every field this investigation's field_assessment relies on (ID/post_name/post_title/permalink/genre/meta.begin_date/end_date/period_string_dates/gamme_de_prix/global_sales_status) and drops only verbose, unused fields (image size variants, full HTML `flexible_content` body) — disclosed here, not silently trimmed. Deliberately includes one genuine multi-day record ('Jarry') and multiple 'Comedy'-genre records alongside real music-genre records.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication); response then bounded to a real subset with disclosed field trimming, per this description

evidence.description: A real, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/olympia-paris.test.mjs, 5 passing tests) re-parsing this investigation's own retained fixture (fixtures/olympia-paris/search-evenements-response-subset.json, identical to the evidence above) via ingestion/olympia-paris/observation-adapter.mjs and reproducing the exact claimed field values deterministically, including the multi-day case and the genre-based music/non-music distinction.
